hook.line: Five secret codes for Claude that you need to know about.
hook.visual: Top half: a blob morphs into the Claude logo on black; bottom half: him at a podcast mic; a white '5 SECRET CLAUDE CODES' label sits on the seam, then an orange flash cuts to B-roll.

beats.what: Morphing blob resolves into the Claude wordmark above his face, list title on the split line
Orange flash transition into office B-roll
Code one typed in huge yellow letters ('L99') over a warped grid above his face
Full-screen scroll of a long Claude answer as proof
Code two '/GHOST' typed in the same yellow-on-warped-grid style
Chat box screen recording with the code typed into the prompt
Screen recording of the Observe/Decide/Act output
Cinematic B-roll of someone at a desk setup for code four
Orange-tinted scroll of a full step-by-step plan, then a final architecture answer for code five

why_it_works: Numbered list of 'secret codes' promises five quick wins, so viewers stay to collect all five
Each code gets the same big yellow typed title, so the structure is readable with sound off
Fast pacing (19.4 cuts/min, median shot 2.2 s) alternates face, title card and proof screen
Every code is followed by a screen of real output, so the claim is shown, not just said
weaknesses: Face visible only about a third of the time (face share 0.304), so the presenter feels secondary
The 'secret codes' framing overstates what are plain prompt prefixes, which can draw skeptical comments
Output screens scroll too fast and too small to read
No CTA at the end; the last frame is black
for_robert: Give each list item the same typed title card over a moving background, with Fred popping in to 'type' it; keep his face on screen more than this creator does.
